newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks slip from peaks, Dow gains cut in half.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks slip from peaks, Dow gains cut in half.

text.p: U.S. stocks slipped from their earlier peaks after news the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting committee decided to leave interest rates unchanged, with the Dow quickly halving a 100-point run-up.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which jumped to a session high of 7905 just seconds before the announcement, quickly dropped to stand at 7858, up 55 points.

"Some investors bought in anticipation of a relief rally after the announcement, but we were already up over 100, so they sold on the news, which really brought the average down in a flash," said Ken Ducey, BT Brokerage director of trading.
"We'll probably stabilize around here. Everybody and their mother was expecting the Fed to do nothing, so it really wasn't anything shocking," he said.

The Standard & Poor's 500 Index, which had been as high as 925, was up seven to 920, a strong gain of about 0.8 percent. The Nasdaq Composite Index was up even more sharply on a percent basis, rising 1.5 percent amid gains of 24 to 1593.
